title: Multi-Scale Modification of Metallic Implants With Pore Gradients, Polyelectrolytes and Their Indirect Monitoring In vivo
protocol: Clean the implants with ethanol.
Sonicate the implants in acetone for 15 min.
Design and manufacture Teflon molds according to the implant size and shape.
Prepare a binary mixture of dioxane and water (87:13%, v:v).
Heat the mixture to 60 °C to obtain a homogenous PLLA solution.
Calculate the volume of the necessary polymer solution based on the porosity of the implant.
Introduce the solution into the implants using precision glass syringes with 0.1 μl accuracy.
Freeze the samples either directly at -80°C or after an incubation period of 30 min at room temperature.
Keep the samples overnight at -80°C.
Immerse the implants in 80% pre-chilled EtOH for extraction.
Carry out the extraction at -20°C overnight.
Extract implants at -20°C overnight.
Remove remaining mold parts from the implants and air dry them.
Perform mercury porosimeter analysis on the implants for overall porosity characterization.
Analyze pore size distribution using Image J with scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Freeze-fracture samples and observe cross-sections with SEM to verify pore gradient.
Label cells within porous implants with PKH26 or Calcein-AM.
Visualize labeled implants with confocal laser microscopy.
Use medical grade collagen type I and sodium alginate for surface coating of implants.
Dip implants in collagen solution at 0.5 g/L concentration in 150 mM NaCl citrate buffer, pH 3.8.
Dip implants in alginate solution at 0.5 g/L concentration in 150 mM NaCl citrate buffer, pH 3.8.
Repeat dipping steps to build multilayers on the implant surface.
Dissolve the collagen solution overnight.
Ensure an acidic pH of 3.8 for stable layer build-up.
Deposit layers by immersing implants into collagen and alginate solutions alternatively using a dipping robot system.
Immerse for 15 min per layer.
Rinse the structure with 150 mM NaCl at pH 3.8 for 5 min between deposition steps.
Design a specific holder for use with dipping robots used in polyelectrolyte multilayer production.
Deposit layers on the surface of titanium only implants or implants modified as described in section 1.
Prepare the crosslinking solution using DMSO and citrate buffer (150 mM NaCl, pH 3.8) at a 1:4 v:v ratio.
Dissolve genipin first in DMSO to avoid clumping, then add water component.
Crosslink samples by immersing them in the crosslinking solution for 12-24 hours.
Rinse samples with copious amounts of citrate buffer (pH 3.8) after crosslinking.
Sterilize the samples with UV treatment for 30 minutes.
Sterilize the samples with an antibiotic/antifungal bath containing Penicillin/Streptomycin and Fungizone.
Calculate fiber diameters using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) images obtained in contact mode.
Dry the samples with a nitrogen flow before imaging.
Quantify the thickness of at least 10 fibers per image to determine the average fibril thickness with Image J software.
Dry (COL/ALG)24 / COL multilayer films.
Use a syringe needle to scratch the film.
Localize the scratch with a light microscope.
Obtain images with AFM on 10 x 10 μm² surfaces at the boundary of the scratch.
Calculate the heights from the profiles obtained with the AFM software to provide the thickness of the film layer.
Carry out the implantation at the target site.
Monitor the general well-being of the animals daily following implantation.
Record the weight of the animals regularly after implantation.
Use western blotting for determination of CGA levels with monoclonal anti-CGA antibodies.
Obtain blood samples from the auricular veins of rabbits.
Centrifuge the collected blood samples at 5,000 rpm for 20 minutes at 4 °C.
Use the supernatant obtained for analysis.
Extract rabbit plasma with 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (1:1; v:v).
Purify the extract using a Dionex HPLC system on a nucleosil reverse-phase column.
Record the absorbance at 214 and 280 nm.
Use a flow rate of 700 μl/min with gradients for elutions.
Collect peak fractions during elutions.
Concentrate fractions by evaporation using speed-vacuum application.
Stop the speed-vacuum before complete dryness is reached.
Correlate peaks obtained at different time-points over the implantation period.
Use purified peptides showing consistent trends for identification.
Load samples to polybrene-treated glass-fibre filters for automatic Edman degradation.
Identify Phenylthiohydantoin-amino acids (Pth-Xaa) by chromatography on a C18 column.
Determine the N-terminal sequence of purified peptides by automatic Edman degradation.
Identify sequences using Blast software with SWISS-Prot database.
